NY-2025-S10732.title: Establishes minority youth-owned business enterprises
NY-2025-S10732.summary: Establishes minority youth-owned business enterprises in the state of New York and the city of New York; creates certain contracting opportunities for members of minority youth-owned business enterprises; establishes an implementation program and oversight committee for minority youth-owned business enterprises.
NY-2025-S10732.aiSummary: The bill would create minority youth-owned business enterprises in New York state and New York City. It would also set up contracting chances for members of these businesses. In addition, it would create a program to carry out the plan and an oversight committee to watch it.

NY-2025-S9977.title: Relates to the Islip Terrace Volunteer Exempt Firefighter's Benevolent Association
NY-2025-S9977.summary: Relates to the Islip Terrace Volunteer Exempt Firefighter's Benevolent Association; makes technical amendments to the chapter incorporating such association.

actions.text: ORDERED TO THIRD READING RULES CAL.607
COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES
AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT

NY-2025-S9977.aiSummary: Makes technical changes to the law that created the Islip Terrace Volunteer Exempt Firefighter's Benevolent Association. The bill passed the Assembly, was sent to the Governor, and was signed into law as chapter 356.

NY-2025-S8276.title: Relates to the qualifications to hold the position of assistant county attorney in the county of Rockland
NY-2025-S8276.summary: Allows a non-resident to hold the position of assistant county attorney in the county of Rockland.

actions.text: REFERRED TO INVESTIGATIONS AND GOVERNMENT OPERATIONS
COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES
REFERRED TO INVESTIGATIONS AND GOVERNMENT OPERATIONS

NY-2025-S8276.aiSummary: The bill would let a person who does not live in Rockland County serve as an assistant county attorney there. It passed the Legislature and was signed into law as Chapter 340.

NY-2025-S10725.title: Requires automated external defibrillators at electric utility worksites
NY-2025-S10725.summary: Requires at least one automated external defibrillator to be available at electric utility worksites where two or more electrical utility workers are performing work on electrical transmission or distribution lines of six hundred one volts or more; requires electric utilities to maintain emergency response plans with regard to the use of automated external defibrillators.
NY-2025-S10725.aiSummary: The bill would require at least one automated external defibrillator to be available at electric utility worksites where two or more utility workers are doing work on high-voltage transmission or distribution lines. It would also require electric utilities to keep emergency response plans for using these devices.

NY-2025-A8796.title: Provides an exemption for certain parcels of land from licensing restrictions for on-premises alcohol consumption for certain manufacturers and wholesalers of alcoholic beverages
NY-2025-A8796.summary: Provides an exemption for certain parcels of land from the licensing restrictions prohibiting manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers of alcoholic beverages from sharing an interest in a licensed premises or to sell at retail for consumption on the premises; provides for the repeal of certain provisions upon expiration thereof.

actions.text: REFERRED TO INVESTIGATIONS AND GOVERNMENT OPERATIONS
REFERENCE CHANGED TO WAYS AND MEANS

NY-2025-A8796.aiSummary: The bill would let certain land parcels get an exemption from rules that limit how alcohol makers, wholesalers, and retailers can share an interest in a licensed place or sell alcohol for drinking on site. It affects certain manufacturers and wholesalers of alcoholic beverages and would end some related rules after a set time.

NY-2025-A10808.title: Relates to automatic license plate reader systems
NY-2025-A10808.summary: Prohibits the use of automatic license plate reader systems or captured plate data by government entities except for certain purposes.

actions.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO CONSUMER AFFAIRS AND PROTECTION
REFERRED TO CONSUMER AFFAIRS AND PROTECTION

NY-2025-A10808.aiSummary: The bill would limit how government agencies use automatic license plate reader systems and the plate data they collect. It would block that use except for certain allowed purposes. It affects government entities that use these systems.

NY-2025-A10052.title: Extends the effectiveness of the authority of the town of Red Hook to impose real estate transfer taxes and to deposit revenue from such taxes into a community preservation fund

actions.text: ORDERED TO THIRD READING RULES CAL.413
REPORTED REFERRED TO WAYS AND MEANS

NY-2025-A10052.aiSummary: The law extends the town of Red Hook’s power to charge a tax on real estate sales and put that money into a community preservation fund. It was signed into law on October 23, 2026. The extension runs through December 31, 2051.

NY-2025-S10718.title: Enacts the "Prader-Willi syndrome residential stabilization and best-practice support act"
NY-2025-S10718.summary: Enacts the "Prader-Willi syndrome residential stabilization and best-practice support act" in relation to providing services to individuals with Prader-Willi syndrome.
NY-2025-S10718.aiSummary: The bill would create the "Prader-Willi syndrome residential stabilization and best-practice support act." It would provide services to people with Prader-Willi syndrome and help support their residential care.

NY-2025-A6836.title: Relates to releasing victims of domestic violence from certain contracts
NY-2025-A6836.summary: Authorizes one or more individuals who are under a shared contract to opt-out of such contract without a fee, penalty or charge due to status as a domestic violence victim; prohibits the company from transferring any contractual or billing responsibility of such shared contract to any other account holders on such shared contract; prevents companies from prohibiting a person who has opted-out due to domestic violence status to enter into a new contract.

actions.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO CORPORATIONS, AUTHORITIES AND COMMISSIONS
REFERRED TO CORPORATIONS, AUTHORITIES AND COMMISSIONS
REFERRED TO CORPORATIONS, AUTHORITIES AND COMMISSIONS

NY-2025-A6836.aiSummary: The bill would let a person on a shared contract leave that contract with no fee, penalty, or charge if they are a domestic violence victim. It would also stop the company from shifting the remaining bill or contract duty to the other people on that shared contract. It would bar the company from refusing to let that person start a new contract later.
